title: Baidu Revenue Falls 6th Quarter as AI Push Struggles
summary: Baidu reports sixth consecutive quarterly revenue decline despite AI investments. Ernie 5.5 Flash Preview launches as company battles Tencent, Alibaba in
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Baidu reported its sixth straight quarterly revenue drop, with Q3 2026 sales falling 1% to $4.6 billion as legacy search advertising weakens.
- The company launched Ernie 5.5 Flash Preview and unveiled a token marketplace, betting on autonomous AI agents to drive future growth.
- Baidu's Ernie models now lag competitors like DeepSeek and Moonshot, while chip spinoff Kunlunxin's Hong Kong IPO may slip into 2027.


Baidu Inc. reported a sixth consecutive quarterly revenue decline on November 16, 2026, as the Chinese internet giant struggles to monetize its AI investments while its core search advertising business continues to erode. Revenue for the three months ended September fell 1% to 30.8 billion yuan ($4.6 billion), meeting analyst expectations but underscoring the urgency of founder Robin Li's pivot to artificial intelligence.


## Legacy Business Pressures Mount


China's once-dominant search leader faces mounting challenges on multiple fronts. Its flagship online advertising business is hemorrhaging users and marketing budgets to newer social platforms, while competitors Tencent Holdings and Alibaba Group have surged ahead in the AI race. Net income for the quarter dropped to 1.4 billion yuan, reflecting the strain of heavy AI infrastructure investments against declining legacy revenues.


The company's Ernie model series, once positioned as China's answer to ChatGPT, has slipped from the top tier of domestic AI offerings. Upstart competitors like DeepSeek and Moonshot have captured developer mindshare with more competitive performance, forcing Baidu to rethink its AI strategy.


## New Model Launch and Strategic Shifts


Officially launched on November 16, 2026, Baidu unveiled Ernie 5.5 Flash Preview, positioning the foundation model for fast inference speeds and competitive pricing. The release comes as the company attempts to regain ground in China's crowded AI marketplace, where differentiation increasingly hinges on cost efficiency and deployment flexibility.


Last week, Baidu introduced a token marketplace designed to connect idle compute capacity with developers seeking access to open-source models. The platform aims to displace traditional middlemen, known as transfer stations in China's AI ecosystem, with accredited providers offering more transparent pricing and service guarantees.


## AI Business Becomes Revenue Majority


Despite the overall revenue contraction, Baidu's AI-driven business now accounts for more than half of total sales, a milestone the company expects to maintain. Billionaire founder Robin Li is betting that a coming surge in autonomous AI agents will create a new ecosystem generating returns on Baidu's cloud computing and chip infrastructure investments.


The company's Apollo Go robotaxi service has expanded to more than 20 cities globally, including fully driverless commercial operations in Dubai. This autonomous driving push represents one of Baidu's clearest paths to AI monetization beyond traditional software licensing.


## Chip Spinoff IPO Uncertainty


Baidu's semiconductor subsidiary Kunlunxin is preparing for an independent listing in Hong Kong, setting up direct competition with Alibaba's T-Head unit, which announced similar IPO plans. However, Bloomberg News reports the market debut could slip into 2027 due to broader market weakness and China's tightened controls on AI-related funding.


The delay would mark another setback for Baidu's strategy to unlock value from its AI infrastructure investments. Kunlunxin's chips power much of Baidu's internal AI workloads, and an independent listing would provide capital for expansion while validating the unit's technology against international competitors.


## What This Means


Baidu's sustained revenue decline illustrates the challenge facing legacy tech giants attempting to transition to AI-first business models. While the company has successfully shifted more than half its revenue to AI-related services, profitability remains elusive as infrastructure costs mount and competition intensifies. The success of Ernie 5.5 Flash Preview and the token marketplace will prove critical in determining whether Baidu can reclaim its position among China's AI leaders or continue ceding ground to more agile competitors. With the Kunlunxin IPO potentially delayed and core search revenues showing no signs of recovery, the company faces mounting pressure to demonstrate that its massive AI investments can deliver sustainable growth beyond 2026.
